statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 15, low, for the 22:00Z reopen hour. CME Globex equity index futures resumed trading at 22:00Z, but no verified Nasdaq-100 print has been published for this slot yet, so the reading prices unpriced weekend-queue risk rather than any observed price structure. Stress is 45, elevated, unchanged from the final pre-reopen hour and held there by last week's bond volatility, WTI at $86.41 and Brent at $93.71 with oil higher for a second consecutive week, and a scheduled US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions at 18:00Z on Monday. Confidence is 82, high: index levels, Treasury yields, the VIX, oil and the week's calendar are all verified against primary sources, while the live reopen price path is not yet observable anywhere. Tail remains below the block threshold across all twenty-four published hours, which carry conditional readings between 6 and 18.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path. The Nasdaq-100 traded a 29,142.44 to 29,405.12 range on Friday and settled at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day though roughly 2% lower on the week, and both session extremes were retraced. The VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.0%, after a 14.77 to 15.95 range. No persistent directional efficiency is on record, and none can be established for the current hour because no verified live futures print exists for it yet. The risk that is present is cross-asset rather than structural: the 10-year Treasury yield finished Friday near 4.73% and the 30-year near 5.27% after a week in which bond volatility, not earnings, drove the index lower; oil has risen more than 5% for a second consecutive week with WTI at $86.41 and Brent at $93.71; and Friday's internals were split, with megacaps mostly higher but the semiconductor complex averaging lower. Those conflicts raise Stress and reduce directional conviction without establishing the failure of mean reversion that Tail measures. The published danger window is kept narrow and covers the reopen hour and the two hours after it, where the weekend headline queue prices.
headline: Futures reopened at 22:00Z with no verified print yet for the slot: Tail 15, low, mapped policy state EA_ON, and conditional readings of 6 to 18 across the next twenty-three hours, peaking at Monday's 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions and the power hour that follows it.
body: CME Globex equity index futures reopened for the week at 22:00Z, roughly half an hour before this assessment. No verified Nasdaq-100 futures print for the reopen is available from any primary source at the time of writing, so no reopen gap, direction or structure is claimed as observed and the current Tail of 15 is a conditional reading covering the unpriced weekend queue rather than a measured price path. The twenty-four published slots run from 2026-08-23T22:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T21:00:00Z: the reopen hour, the overnight Asian and European sessions, the full Monday US cash session, and the 21:00Z CME daily maintenance break at the end. Monday's 12:30Z Chicago Fed National Activity Index, the 13:30Z US cash open, the 15:30Z bill auctions, the 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions, the power hour that follows it and the 20:00Z cash close all fall inside the horizon. The last observed session was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33%, inside a 29,142.44 to 29,405.12 range whose extremes were both retraced, and the VIX finished at 14.89. The week itself was negative, with the Nasdaq Composite down about 2% and the S&P 500 down about 1.4%, driven by Treasury market volatility rather than by index earnings; the 10-year finished near 4.73% and the 30-year near 5.27%. Oil is the second standing amplifier, with WTI at $86.41 and Brent at $93.71 after a second consecutive week of gains above 5%, supported by US-Iran sanctions escalation and Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context shows megacaps mostly higher on Friday while the semiconductor complex averaged lower, an internal conflict that reduces directional conviction. That combination raises Stress and lowers Confidence without meeting the standard for a Tail amplifier, which requires observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed retracements, or repeated extension. None of those is on record. The week ahead adds PCE and the second-estimate GDP on Wednesday, Nvidia results after Wednesday's close, and the Jackson Hole keynote and preliminary payrolls benchmark revision on Friday.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past twenty-four hours is nearly complete: twenty hourly assessments are available and four clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable, at 07:00Z, 10:00Z, 11:00Z and 12:00Z on 23 August. Across every available hour Tail held 4, the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON and the dominant mode remained normal, so no hour approached the block threshold. Those readings all fell inside the weekend futures halt, when no Nasdaq-100 price path could develop at all. Stress traced a full weekend arc, easing from 40 at the start of the window to a low of 34 through the European morning, then turning higher across the afternoon and evening to 45 in the final pre-reopen hour as the unpriced weekend headline queue built. Confidence drifted down gently from 87 to 84 over the same span as the last verified price observation receded further into the past.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail 15 and Stress 45 for the reopen itself, on unpriced weekend-queue risk rather than observed structure, because no verified live print exists for the slot. Conditional Tail then eases through the first hours after the reopen, from 14 to 12 as Tokyo supplies the first genuine regional liquidity of the week, and settles at a floor of 10 through the quiet Asian mid-session where two-way trade has historically been most reliable. It steps back to 13 at the 07:00Z European cash open, the session's first real liquidity event and the point at which any weekend gap is confirmed or faded, then eases again through a quiet European late morning. The 12:30Z Chicago Fed release is treated as a checkpoint at Tail 12. The Monday US cash open inside the 13:00Z hour carries 16 for opening-auction continuation risk, easing to 15 and then 13 across the auction window. The arc peaks at 18 for the 18:00Z US Treasury news conference on new Iran sanctions and holds 18 through the power hour that follows, where a delayed second leg running from oil into yields and then equities is the credible mechanism; both slots carry the event/whipsaw mode and both remain below the block threshold, because event importance before a print raises Stress and lowers Confidence rather than establishing a no-retracement path. The final two slots step down to 14 for the cash close and 6 for the CME daily maintenance break, where little tradable interval exists. Confidence decays steadily from 82 to 58 across the horizon as distance from the last verified observation grows.
